compiled_state.title: As a DSO maintainer, I can attribute each bug to its detection channel (tests, review, production, etc.) so the program's headline 'caught-by-tests rate' is computable
compiled_state.author: Test
compiled_state.description:
## Context

The calibration program's headline success metric — 'what fraction of bugs are caught by tests vs other channels?' — is uncomputable today because bug tickets carry no detection-channel attribution. 4911-c7ba's bug-classification taxonomy classifies bugs by TYPE (the 27-slug bug-type-<slug> taxonomy) but not by DETECTION CHANNEL. This story surfaced during the calibration program observability gap analysis as the highest-priority program-critical measurement gap.

## What

Add a detected_by classification dimension to the bug-ticket schema with the following allowed values:
- tests — caught by a test failing (CI or local test run); mutation-testing breaches from 411b-a047 set this value
- review-llm — caught during /dso:review (LLM reviewer dimension)
- review-human — caught during human PR review
- production — caught by user/system in production or deployed environment
- user-report — user-reported, channel not otherwise specified
- internal-dogfood — caught during internal dogfooding / pre-production usage
- other — any channel not above; bug description must include rationale

## Touchpoints (resolved during implementation-plan)

- plugins/dso/skills/shared/prompts/bug-report-template.md — add detected_by field documentation with allowed values
- plugins/dso/skills/create-bug/SKILL.md — guide ticket creators to set the field; integrate into the dialogue
- /dso:fix-bug Phase G — when filing a NEGATIVE_EXAMPLE-tagged bug, set detected_by appropriately
- 411b-a047 auto-bug-creation logic (CI mutation-testing workflow) — set detected_by: tests for mutation-testing-breach bugs
- 69e8-af39 retro Graduation Phase — use detected_by as a graduation-candidate weighting signal (production-caught and review-caught bugs are higher-value graduation candidates than test-caught bugs)
- Tag application: detected_by:<channel> tag set on each bug for ticket-CLI searchability via ticket list --has-tag=detected_by:<channel>

## Why this is needed now

Without this attribution, the calibration program's central success claim cannot be measured. The brainstorm session that produced the six calibration epics surfaced this gap during a post-brainstorm observability analysis. Implementing this small addition before the calibration program epics begin shipping ensures that bug data from the start of the program is correctly attributed and trend analysis is meaningful.

## Sketch of done definitions

- bug-report-template.md documents the detected_by field with allowed values verbatim from the list above
- /dso:create-bug or equivalent dialogue elicits the field at bug-ticket creation time and applies the corresponding detected_by:<channel> tag
- ticket list --has-tag=detected_by:tests returns the set of test-caught bugs (including 411b's auto-created bugs)
- 411b's auto-bug-creation logic sets detected_by: tests (and corresponding tag)
- 69e8's graduation phase has visibility into detected_by tags via the standard ticket query
- Existing closed bugs without a detected_by tag default to 'other' for backward compatibility (no retroactive migration required)

Coordination: 411b and 69e8's auto-bug-creation flows must be updated when this story ships to set detected_by appropriately. Ticket comments on those epics noting the dependency.

comments.body: Closing — scope rolled into the new Calibration Program Observability epic where channel attribution naturally fits as a measurement primitive. Avoids preplanning reconciliation risk under 4911-c7ba (which owns bug-TYPE taxonomy, not detection-CHANNEL).
comments.author: Test
